answer: A reputation bond makes a Sybil attack expensive: before an agent can join a voyage of trades, it must lock a refundable stake at the network jetty, the shared entry point where identities are issued. Each stake is tied to one verified key, and misbehavior burns it. Like a dune that shifts under every step, the cost grows with each fake identity an attacker piles up, so creating thousands of sock-puppet agents costs thousands of stakes, while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
